post.description:
Requires an Organization Key. Shares Console End User field rules. With an externalId exactly equal (after trimming) to that of an End User of this Organization, whichever surface created it, returns that End User unchanged with 200: request fields are not applied and a disabled End User is returned with its status. An externalId equal to another only under the case- and accent-insensitive comparison (which also equates forms such as ß and ss) returns 409. Otherwise creates the End User and returns 201; without an externalId every request creates a new End User. Retrying a creation with the same externalId is safe, and concurrent creations with one new externalId create one End User. Creation atomically copies the Organization initial personal monthly LLM ceiling when one is configured; otherwise the User has no personal ceiling. Creates no Platform Account, Membership, Agent or management authority. Save user.userId as your application mapping.

Authorization: OrganizationApiKey; persisted credentials determine Organization and End User scope.

200.description: A persisted Server-Sent Events stream under current exact Organization Key, ordinary User, and Organization authority. Revocation or rotation closes only that credential’s subscription; disabled ordinary owners remain readable. The cursor in each id field can be supplied on a later request. Disconnecting the subscription does not cancel the active Turn. Each data frame is a JSON envelope with type, sessionId, turnId, createdAt and data. Turn events (agent.session.turn.*) carry the durable Turn event in data. Terminal Template switches arrive as agent.session.template_switch.succeeded or agent.session.template_switch.failed with display-safe command, status, epoch and Template provenance. Realtime facts of the Session timeline arrive in the same order: agent.session.realtime.input_transcript.completed for each final user transcript and agent.session.realtime.response.completed for each completed Realtime model response, with data {id, type, realtimeConnectionId, text, turnId, createdAt} and, for a response, kind (chat, task_ack, task_progress, task_result, clarify; historical device_ack remains readable), responseId and interrupted. Their envelope turnId is the linked Turn or null. Partial Realtime transcripts are delivered only on the realtime connection. agent.session.turn.output_text.snapshot carries the complete provisional draft in data.payload.text: replace the draft for that turnId, including revisions or an empty reset, rather than appending. A resumed snapshot is independently usable without earlier draft frames. agent.session.turn.progress carries a separate progress message in data.payload.text. agent.session.turn.item.added with data.event = assistant_message carries the final saved message in data.payload.text and data.payload.messageId; the terminal Turn event establishes its outcome. agent.session.turn.item.added with data.event = operation_step carries data.payload.operationId, status and label; a tool Operation also carries data.payload.category (skill_read for a read inside a frozen Skill package, with data.payload.skill {skillId, name}; otherwise tool_call), matching the Operation in Turn reads. Client Tool progress also carries safe data.payload.source: {type: session_client} or {type: hardware, hardwareBindingId, method}. Historical calls may carry hardwareRequirementId. Hardware labels identify the binding or requirement and original method. Hardware arguments, outputs and private target identities are omitted from progress and Turn Operations. The hardware_read_state platform tool creates a hardware.state.read Operation; public input contains only its tool name and binding or requirement identifier, and output omits sensor data. Metadata-only Operations omit source. Events saved before these fields existed omit them. agent.session.turn.requires_action with data.event = client_tool_calls carries data.payload.calls, the Client Tool calls of one model step, each with callId, name, arguments and deadlineAt; answer each with agent.session.input.client_tool_output before its deadline. Receiving this event counts as delivery of its calls. No output_text.delta alias is emitted.

200.description: An idempotent replay of an already accepted command.

202.description: The command was accepted. Message and cancellation commands return durable interaction receipts; retry commands return a retrying event receipt. Execution progress is delivered separately by GET /events.

400.description: The command envelope or command data is invalid, or an idle text Turn admission exceeds the combined Session-client and Hardware tool limit after model projection (64 tools or 64 KiB; validation_failed). Admission saves no input or Turn on this overflow. New checkpoint retries are disabled by default and return checkpoint_runtime_unavailable when disabled or unavailable; previously accepted retry commands still recover their receipts.

404.description: The Session is unavailable or authorization-hidden, or a client_tool_output references an unknown, foreign or Hardware call (client_tool_call_unavailable).

409.description: The command identity was already used with a different body or target state, a new message or retry targets a read-only Session (session_read_only), a checkpoint retry targets an earlier Session Configuration Epoch (session_configuration_epoch_changed), or a Session Template switch is in progress (session_switch_in_progress).

503.description: New Turn admission is temporarily closed for deployment maintenance or recovery (turn_admission_closed), or the deployment lacks the Sandbox or Drive9 service a new Turn needs (service_configuration_unavailable; details.reason names it). This refusal happens before the command is saved, so the same clientEventId can be sent again once the service is set up. If the configuration changes after that check, the command is accepted instead and its Turn fails with the same code and reason in turn_error. A model the deployment does not configure keeps its 409 model_provider_unconfigured refusal.

effectiveDefaultModel.description: Suggested default for new Sessions: the active release default when selectable, else the Organization default when selectable, else the first selectable model. Session creation without a model applies only the first two and otherwise refuses with model_provider_unconfigured.

organizationAllowedModels.description: Stored Organization allow-list. It does not currently limit selection.

effectiveAllowedModels.description: Models the Organization can select now: every model the active release serves.

BillingTag.description: A non-secret attribution label. The pair is matched exactly and is not an authorization boundary.

key.description: Case-sensitive key: a lowercase ASCII letter followed by up to 63 lowercase ASCII letters, digits, underscores, dots, or hyphens.

value.description: Case-sensitive value normalized to NFC and limited to 1–128 bytes in UTF-8. Leading or trailing Unicode whitespace and Unicode control or format characters are rejected.

ClarificationItem.description: A structured blocking question and its optional canonical persisted response. The linked user Message remains the readable conversation projection.

selectionMode.description: Requires exactly one answer and two or three mutually exclusive candidates.

answerChoices.description: Candidate display order is also the canonical structured-answer order.

selectionMode.description: Accepts a non-empty selection containing candidate values and/or at most one user-supplied value, with two through eight compatible candidates.

answerChoices.description: Candidate display order is also the canonical structured-answer order.

answers.description: Distinct structured values in candidate display order, followed by at most one user-supplied answer.

ClientToolOperationSource.description: Client Tool source; only safe requirement and original method are exposed for Hardware. Absent on metadata-only Operations. Current reads default older Session-client Operations to session_client; persisted historical progress events may omit source.

displayName.description: Optional field, trimmed before enforcing 1–255 characters. Whitespace-only values are rejected.

externalId.description: Optional field, trimmed before enforcing 1–255 characters. Whitespace-only values are rejected.

billingTag.description: One immutable Billing Tag snapshot for this resource. Null means untagged; request fields may be omitted only where the operation documents inheritance.

tools.description: Client Tools this Session client declares and executes; each client-started Turn uses the set current at its admission.

name.description: Client function name; platform tool names including hardware_read_state, the mcp_ prefix and double underscores are reserved.

hardwareIds.description: Distinct Hardware IDs with an active Registration for the Session owner. All bindings and the Session commit together.

interrupted.description: The reply was interrupted; its transcript may include speech the user did not hear.

MessageInputContext.description: Server-recorded channel of a user input; clients cannot set it. Present on user Messages except Scheduler-triggered Turns and Messages saved before it existed; absent on assistant Messages. Tolerate channel values added later.

utterance.description: Transcript of the user's own speech when the Message content is a task delegated from it.

emotion.description: Emotion the Realtime model perceived in the speech; not a verified fact.

realtimeSummary.description: Legacy field on Messages saved by earlier releases; new Messages omit it. The Realtime model's own summary of the preceding voice conversation; model-written, not a durable transcript.

oneOf.description: A Realtime Standing Task cycle: the platform started this Turn with the Template's standing goal while a Realtime Connection was live; nobody typed or spoke it.

audio.description: Client audio formats, chosen independently per direction; mono only. Input: pcm16 8000 or 16000 Hz (default), or opus 16000 Hz with packetDurationMs 20 (default), 40 or 60. Output: pcm16 8000, 16000 or 24000 Hz (default), or opus 24000 Hz with packetDurationMs 20 and fixed bitrate 16000, 24000 or 32000 bps (default 32000). bitrate is accepted only on opus output. PCM16 8000 Hz input is resampled to 16000 Hz, and 24000 Hz provider output to the selected lower PCM16 rate, when required; 8000 Hz has telephone quality and can reduce recognition accuracy. Anything else, or a format the configured Realtime model cannot be served with, answers 400 audio_format_unsupported with one detail per refused direction, naming its first unsupported field.

packetDurationMs.description: Opus only: the duration of each packet; one packet travels in one audio frame.

bitrate.description: Opus output only: fixed bitrate in bps, 16000, 24000 or 32000 (default). Rejected on input and pcm16. Unsupported numeric values answer 400 audio_format_unsupported.

packetDurationMs.description: Opus only: the duration of each packet; one packet travels in one audio frame.

bitrate.description: Opus output only: fixed bitrate in bps, 16000, 24000 or 32000 (default). Rejected on input and pcm16. Unsupported numeric values answer 400 audio_format_unsupported.

metadata.description: Client string metadata, stored verbatim and echoed on the Realtime connection.

realtimeConnection.description: A Realtime connection of the Session. status connecting: admitted, but no WebSocket has connected yet; active: the realtime stream is open; paused: a task waits for the user to answer a clarification question; ended: terminal.

websocketUrl.description: WebSocket URL of /api/v1/user/sessions/{id}/realtime/ws. Open it with subprotocol tidb-link.realtime.v1 and send session.connect with connectToken as the first frame.

connectToken.description: One-time connect token. It authorizes exactly one session.connect on any replica and needs no API key, so a customer backend can hand it to a device.

connectTokenExpiresAt.description: When the connect token expires: 60 seconds after it was minted.

kind.description: Historical long-term Memory Operations remain records only.

backend.description: Historical long-term Memory Operations may retain the `mem9` backend value.

targetKind.description: Historical long-term Memory Operations may retain the `memory` target kind.

category.description: How to group a tool Operation: skill_read when it reads a file inside one of its AgentRun's frozen Skill packages, whether Runtime loaded the Skill instructions or the model read a package file; tool_call for every other tool Operation. Absent on non-tool Operations such as llm.complete and on metadata-only Operations.

input.description: Kind-specific input. Hardware Client Tool Operations expose only toolName, callId and mode, omitting device arguments.

output.description: Hardware Client Tool Operations omit output in every status. Kind-specific result. An llm.complete Operation exposes usage as token counts only: input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, totalTokens, and optional cacheWrite1h and reasoning. Counts that are unavailable or invalid are omitted; absent usage is omitted. Supplier SDK cost is not exposed. Customer fees are available from the Billing usage APIs. A failed or interrupted llm.complete Operation has error {code, message, details?} with fixed text only; model_provider_failed carries details.provider (category, (category, httpStatus, errorType, errorCode); other failures use runtime_error or a ledger outcome code. Any other failed, interrupted or unknown_result Operation with an error, including tool Operations, has error {code, message, details} with fixed text naming only the tool: an intentional tool code (for example mcp_unavailable or validation_error) is kept; an allow-listed web_search_* or session_recall_* reason becomes the code and is repeated as details.code with a boolean details.retryable; anything else reads tool_failed. A memory.recall Operation keeps only memory_recall_failed, turn_interrupted or operation_result_unknown, and otherwise reads tool_failed. details also carries tool, category (rejected, unavailable, remote_error, failed, unknown_result, interrupted or unexpected) and, when known, dispatch and retryContract.

label.description: Readable Hardware Client Tool label, for example Speaker · set_volume. Absent on metadata-only Operations.

category.description: How to group a tool Operation: skill_read when it reads a file inside one of its AgentRun's frozen Skill packages, whether Runtime loaded the Skill instructions or the model read a package file; tool_call for every other tool Operation. Absent on non-tool Operations such as llm.complete and on metadata-only Operations.

skill.description: The Skill a skill_read Operation read from; present only with category skill_read.

source.description: Client Tool source. Hardware exposes the Session binding or historical requirement identifier and original method. Private device and Registration identities are omitted. Absent on metadata-only Operations. Current reads default older Session-client Operations to session_client; persisted historical progress events may omit source.

label.description: Readable Hardware Client Tool label, for example Speaker · set_volume. Absent on metadata-only Operations.

input.description: Kind-specific input. A tool Operation has toolName and args; a Hardware Client Tool exposes only toolName, callId and mode, omitting device arguments. Neither input nor output carries the model supplier's tool-call id; use the Operation id to identify a tool call and its result.

output.description: Kind-specific result. Hardware Client Tool Operations omit output in every status. An llm.complete Operation exposes usage as token counts only: input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, totalTokens, and optional cacheWrite1h and reasoning. Counts that are unavailable or invalid are omitted; absent usage is omitted. Supplier SDK cost is not exposed. Customer fees are available from the Billing usage APIs. A failed or interrupted llm.complete Operation has error {code, message, details?} with fixed text only; model_provider_failed carries details.provider (category, httpStatus, errorType, errorCode); other failures use runtime_error or a ledger outcome code. Any other failed, interrupted or unknown_result Operation with an error, including tool Operations, has error {code, message, details} with fixed text naming only the tool: an intentional tool code (for example mcp_unavailable or validation_error) is kept; an allow-listed web_search_* or session_recall_* reason becomes the code and is repeated as details.code with a boolean details.retryable; anything else reads tool_failed. A memory.recall Operation keeps only memory_recall_failed, turn_interrupted or operation_result_unknown, and otherwise reads tool_failed. details also carries tool, category (rejected, unavailable, remote_error, failed, unknown_result, interrupted or unexpected) and, when known, dispatch and retryContract.
